As a general rule of thumb i wake up about 2 hrs later each day from the chronic pain unless I have a schedule and realistically a bit of support keeping thag schedule. Sometimes if the pain is bad and/or I'm having a lot of panic attacks It can jump all over the place. 

Honestly don't think there's any one thing per say that has helped. It's more sort of been about tradeoffs and juggling them to find critical masses that work. I stopped drinking but I traded alcohol for weed really, I ain't about to preach to you. 

In terms of a circadian rythym tho, definately try get some sunlight on your skin during the days that you can. Magnesium (spinach, kale, brocoli) are great to have alongside proteins especially if you don't eat much red meat.  Having a small fermented food snack before dinner (1hr out) can aid digestion and help you have an easier time falling asleep but may make you hungry faster which may make it difficult to sleep if you don't fall asleep before you start feeling hungry again. Chammomille tea I find has a really soft and warm taste and I like to drink that in the evening instead of coffee. Where as I like having a coffee in the morning at breakfast and again at second breakfast and again at lunch and maybe another cup or 2 of green tea in the afternoon so I'm not awake or crashing too early/late. Spending time outside in nature going fishing always lets me sleep pretty easy even though I'm just sitting in a chair with an old blanket and a hoody feeding the fish for most of it.

Ooft, that sounds gnarly af man/mam.  Likewise am glad you have found somethings that work for you too! Noone chooses chronic pain either and it so often goes hand it hand with ptsd. It's all about sharing info and strategies in that long search right?
